models.name: AASIST
models.summary: Raw-waveform sinc filters and residual encoder, then spectral and temporal graph attention joined by a max graph operation; trained on ASVspoof 2019 LA only.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows, SincNet-style filters and residual encoder, spectral and temporal graph attention with a max graph operation, two-way classifier
models.description: AASIST (Jung et al., ICASSP 2022) builds graphs over spectral and temporal nodes of a learned time-frequency map and combines them with heterogeneous graph attention, so one model covers artefacts that earlier work needed an ensemble for. The released weights saw only the ASVspoof 2019 LA training split, with no pretraining. A compact single-corpus baseline that sits near chance on In-the-Wild.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: AASIST: Audio Anti-Spoofing Using Integrated Spectro-Temporal Graph Attention Networks

models.why: The most-cited open audio detector, trained only on English ASVspoof speech: it stands for the off-the-shelf detector a South Asian platform would deploy today, and is the classic half of the probe's audio pair.

models.name: AASIST3
models.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (repo LICENSE; the model card says CC BY-NC 4.0)
models.summary: AASIST on wav2vec 2.0 XLSR-53 features with Kolmogorov-Arnold (KAN) layers; the released weights are not the paper's and are weak.
models.architecture: Pre-emphasised 16 kHz window, wav2vec 2.0 XLSR-53 features, KAN bridge and residual encoder, spectral and temporal graph attention, four inference branches, KAN output layer, two-way classifier
models.description: AASIST3 (Borodin et al., 2024), built for ASVspoof 5, feeds XLSR-53 features into AASIST and replaces some layers with KAN layers. The released weights saw ASVspoof 2019 LA, ASVspoof 5, MLAAD and M-AILABS on a front end pretrained on Common Voice, BABEL and Multilingual LibriSpeech, so the contamination guard refuses it on MLAAD-based evalsets. The repository says these are not the weights behind the paper's numbers, and the model card's Speech Arena re-scoring puts them far lower, so treat it as a weak multilingual baseline; parity is not checked yet.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: AASIST3: KAN-Enhanced AASIST Speech Deepfake Detection using SSL Features and Additional Regularization for the ASVspoof 2024 Challenge

published.cite: Table 1, ensemble with extra data; not the released weights

models.why: Picked as the only AASIST variant trained with multilingual fakes (MLAAD, which has Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Urdu and Sinhala). The released weights aren't the paper's and score far below it, so they can't answer that question, and the guard refuses them on every MLAAD evalset.

models.name: AASIST-L
models.summary: The lightweight AASIST configuration (about 85k parameters): same raw-waveform graph attention, trained on ASVspoof 2019 LA only.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows, SincNet-style filters and residual encoder, spectral and temporal graph attention with a max graph operation, two-way classifier (lightweight configuration)
models.description: AASIST-L is the reduced configuration from the AASIST paper (Jung et al., ICASSP 2022), with the same architecture at a fraction of the width. The released weights saw only the ASVspoof 2019 LA training split. The cheapest single-corpus baseline here; like AASIST it is near chance on In-the-Wild.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: AASIST: Audio Anti-Spoofing Using Integrated Spectro-Temporal Graph Attention Networks

models.why: Picked as the phone-sized AASIST, for detection on cheap devices. On every South Asian set so far it scores within a few hundredths of AASIST, so it shows nothing the bigger model doesn't.

models.name: AltFreezing
models.summary: 3D CNN on face clips whose spatial and temporal weight groups are frozen alternately in training, so it learns both cue types; FF++. Blocked.
models.architecture: Face video clip, 3D convolutional network whose spatial and temporal weight groups are frozen alternately during training, two-way classifier
models.description: AltFreezing (Wang et al., CVPR 2023) counters a 3D CNN's tendency to rely on either spatial or temporal cues by training the two weight groups in alternation. The released weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (compression not stated). Blocked here: the weights are only on RecDrive and Baidu, upstream issues report the file gone, and there is no adapter.

paper.title: AltFreezing for More General Video Face Forgery Detection

models.why: The probe's temporal video detector: talking heads and lip-sync fakes are edited over time, and frame models can miss motion artefacts. Blocked until someone can fetch its weights.

models.name: AntiDeepfake MMS-300M
models.summary: MMS-300M wav2vec 2.0 front end, mean pooling and a linear head, post-trained on 74k hours of real and fake speech in over 100 languages.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows (zero mean, unit variance), MMS-300M wav2vec 2.0 front end, mean pooling over frames, linear layer, two-way classifier
models.description: AntiDeepfake (Ge et al., NII Yamagishi Lab, 2025) inserts a post-training stage on real and fake speech between SSL pretraining and task fine-tuning. This model starts from MMS-300M (pretrained on about 1,400 languages) and is post-trained on 74k hours from 29 corpora in over 100 languages, including FLEURS, MLAAD, all of ASVspoof 2019 LA, LJSpeech and VoxCeleb2. The broadest multilingual exposure of any audio model here, so the contamination guard refuses it on MLAAD-based evalsets and anything built from FLEURS.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: Post-training for Deepfake Speech Detection

models.why: Half of the cleanest test of the language question: the same post-training as the w2v2 small model on a backbone pretrained on about 1,400 languages. Its post-training heard Hindi, Bengali, Urdu, Tamil and Nepali but no Sinhala, so a Sinhala set would show what an unheard South Asian language does.

models.name: AntiDeepfake wav2vec 2.0 small
models.summary: English-pretrained wav2vec 2.0 base (95M parameters) with the same AntiDeepfake post-training; the cheap counterpart to MMS-300M.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows (zero mean, unit variance), wav2vec 2.0 base front end, mean pooling over frames, linear layer, two-way classifier
models.description: The smallest AntiDeepfake model (Ge et al., 2025): wav2vec 2.0 base pretrained on LibriSpeech only, post-trained on the same 74k hours from 29 corpora as the MMS-300M model, with mean pooling and one linear layer. Identical post-training data make the pair a controlled test of multilingual pretraining. The contamination guard refuses it on MLAAD-based evalsets and anything built from FLEURS.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: Post-training for Deepfake Speech Detection

published.cite: results table; paper Table II gives 4.23%

models.why: The other half of that pair: the same post-training on an English-only backbone, so its gap to MMS-300M on South Asian speech comes from the pretraining languages alone.

models.name: CORE
models.summary: Xception frame classifier trained with a consistency loss between representations of augmented views; DeepfakeBench weights, FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, Xception CNN trained with a consistency loss across augmented views, two-way classifier
models.description: CORE (Ni et al., CVPRW 2022) penalises the distance between representations of differently augmented views of a face (crops, colour changes) to reduce overfitting; at test time it is a plain Xception frame classifier. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23 per the DeepfakeBench README) after ImageNet pretraining. It differs from the Xception baseline only in the training loss.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: CORE: Consistent Representation Learning for Face Forgery Detection

models.why: Trained for representations that stay consistent across augmented views, so it tests whether that robustness survives South Asian faces and the recompression of forwarded clips. Like every DeepfakeBench detector here it trained on FF++, so each reads a different cue on the same faces; second tier, worth running once South Asian video arrives.

models.name: DF Arena 1B
models.licence: non-commercial (custom LICENSE.txt in the model repo)
models.summary: XLS-R 1B front end, attention pooling over every hidden layer and a conformer head; the top open model on the Speech DF Arena.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows, XLS-R 1B front end, attention pooling over every hidden layer, conformer head, spoof or bona fide classifier
models.description: Released by the team behind the Speech DF Arena leaderboard (Speech-Arena-2025). The XLS-R front end was pretrained on Common Voice, BABEL, MLS, VoxPopuli and VoxLingua107, and the detector trained on ASVspoof 2019 and 2024, MLAAD, Codecfake, LibriSeVoc, DFADD, CtrSVDD, SpoofCeleb and EnvSDD. The contamination guard therefore refuses it on ASVspoof 2019 LA eval and MLAAD-based evalsets.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: Speech DF Arena: A Leaderboard for Speech DeepFake Detection Models

published.cite: evaluation table; trained on its train split

models.why: The strongest open audio detector, so it sets the ceiling South Asian results are read against. Its training includes MLAAD, whose generators recur in South Asian sets, so part of its score there may be familiarity.

models.name: DF Arena 500M
models.licence: non-commercial (custom LICENSE.txt in the model repo)
models.summary: The XLS-R 300M sibling of DF Arena 1B: same all-layer attention pooling, conformer head and broad training mix.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows, XLS-R 300M front end, attention pooling over every hidden layer, conformer head, spoof or bona fide classifier
models.description: Same design and training data as DF Arena 1B (Speech-Arena-2025) with the smaller XLS-R 300M front end, pretrained on Common Voice, BABEL, MLS, VoxPopuli and VoxLingua107; the detector saw ASVspoof 2019 and 2024, MLAAD, Codecfake, LibriSeVoc, DFADD, CtrSVDD, SpoofCeleb and EnvSDD. The contamination guard refuses it on ASVspoof 2019 LA eval and MLAAD-based evalsets.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: Speech DF Arena: A Leaderboard for Speech DeepFake Detection Models

published.cite: evaluation table; trained on its train split

models.why: Picked to test whether size helps on South Asian speech. The 1B model isn't consistently better, so with that reported the smaller one is redundant.

models.name: EfficientNet-B4
models.summary: Plain EfficientNet-B4 frame classifier on aligned face crops; DeepfakeBench's single-network version, trained on FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, EfficientNet-B4 CNN, two-way classifier
models.description: DeepfakeBench's single-network version of the detector studied by Bonettini et al. (ICPR 2020), whose paper ensembles several EfficientNet-B4 variants. The weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23 per the DeepfakeBench README) after ImageNet pretraining. With Xception it is the plain-CNN video baseline, with no forgery-specific cue.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Video Face Manipulation Detection Through Ensemble of CNNs

models.why: Picked as a second classic video baseline beside Xception. It reads the same texture cue from the same FF++ training, so it is unlikely to show anything about South Asian faces that Xception doesn't.

models.name: Effort
models.licence: none published (README badge says CC BY-NC 4.0; issue 3 asks for a licence file)
models.summary: CLIP ViT-L/14 adapted by SVD: principal singular components frozen, residual tuned; DeepfakeBench detector on FF++ c23. Blocked on weights.
models.architecture: Aligned 224 px face crop, CLIP ViT-L/14 image encoder with SVD-split weights (principal part frozen, residual part tuned), linear head
models.description: Effort (Yan et al., ICML 2025) splits each weight matrix by SVD, freezes the principal subspace and trains only the residual, which the authors argue stops fine-tuning from collapsing the feature space onto a few fake patterns. The paper targets AI-generated images broadly; here DeepfakeBench's Effort detector, trained on FaceForensics++ (c23) after CLIP pretraining on OpenAI's private data, scores face frames. Blocked since Google Drive refused the weight file as over quota on 2026-10-05; upstream also reports a Celeb-DF v2 reproduction gap and has no licence file.
models.input: 224 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

models.why: The probe's original foundation-model video detector, the partner to Xception. Blocked on weights; GenD holds its place until they arrive.

models.name: F3Net
models.summary: DCT frequency-band decomposition (12 input channels) into Xception, for artefacts that survive compression; DeepfakeBench weights, FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, DCT frequency-band decomposition (12 input channels), Xception CNN, two-way classifier
models.description: F3Net (Qian et al., ECCV 2020) splits each face crop into frequency bands with a discrete cosine transform and classifies the bands with Xception, since manipulation traces persist there after video compression. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23) after ImageNet pretraining. The detector's yaml names only NeuralTextures, which may not describe the checkpoint; the benchmark treats it as trained on all of FF++.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Thinking in Frequency: Face Forgery Detection by Mining Frequency-aware Clues

models.why: Reads frequency bands chosen to survive compression, the cue most likely to matter for South Asian clips that circulate recompressed on messaging apps. Like every DeepfakeBench detector here it trained on FF++, so each reads a different cue on the same faces; second tier, worth running once South Asian video arrives.

models.name: FFD
models.summary: Xception with a learned attention map over manipulated regions that reweights features before classification; DeepfakeBench weights, FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, Xception CNN with an attention map over manipulated regions, two-way classifier
models.description: FFD (Dang et al., CVPR 2020) estimates an attention map of manipulated face regions and uses it to reweight the feature maps; the map doubles as a coarse forgery localisation. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23 per the DeepfakeBench README) after ImageNet pretraining. Passes parity against the original code.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: On the Detection of Digital Face Manipulation

models.why: Learns where on the face the manipulation is, so it shows whether its attention transfers to South Asian faces. Like every DeepfakeBench detector here it trained on FF++, so each reads a different cue on the same faces; second tier, worth running once South Asian video arrives.

models.name: GenD (CLIP ViT-L/14)
models.summary: CLIP ViT-L/14 with only LayerNorm tuned, L2-normalised features and metric learning; frame probabilities averaged per video. Trained on FF++.
models.architecture: Aligned face crop at native size, CLIP ViT-L/14 image encoder with only LayerNorm parameters tuned, L2-normalised features, linear head
models.description: GenD (Yermakov et al., WACV 2026) tunes only CLIP's LayerNorm parameters (about 0.03% of the model), constrains features to the hypersphere with L2 normalisation and metric learning, and averages per-frame P(fake) over the video. The released weights were trained on FaceForensics++ only, after CLIP pretraining on OpenAI's private image-text data. The main generalisation-first video model here; the adapter runs end to end but parity is not checked yet.
models.input: native-size aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Deepfake Detection that Generalizes Across Benchmarks

models.why: The foundation-model half of the video pair, in Effort's place. Its backbone was pretrained on far more varied faces than FF++, which tests whether that removes skin-tone bias; on HiDF it flagged real Indian faces most often, so it is the first model to check on South Asian faces.

models.name: GenD (Perception Encoder L/14)
models.summary: The GenD recipe (LayerNorm-only tuning, L2-normalised features) on Meta's Perception Encoder L/14 instead of CLIP.
models.architecture: Aligned face crop at native size resized to 224, Meta Perception Encoder L/14 with only LayerNorm parameters tuned, L2-normalised features, linear head
models.description: GenD's second released backbone (Yermakov et al., WACV 2026): identical training on Perception Encoder, so the pair isolates the effect of the foundation model. Trained on FaceForensics++ only; Meta's pretraining data are not public, so overlap with our data cannot be checked. Parity is not checked yet.
models.input: native-size aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Deepfake Detection that Generalizes Across Benchmarks

models.why: The same GenD recipe on Meta's Perception Encoder instead of CLIP: whether the pretraining behind the backbone changes how it treats South Asian faces. Second tier, run beside GenD (CLIP).

models.name: HAVIC
models.summary: Audio and video transformers pretrained on real videos for audio-visual coherence, fused to score 16-frame windows; fine-tuned on FakeAVCeleb.
models.architecture: 16-frame windows of 224 px face frames plus 128-bin audio filterbank, audio and video transformer encoders pretrained on real videos, audio-visual interaction module, MLP classifier, one logit per window
models.description: HAVIC (CVPR 2026 Findings) pretrains its audio and video encoders on real videos only (LRS2) to model temporal and cross-modal coherence, then fuses them to score clips whose lips, voice or expression disagree. It was fine-tuned on a random 70% of FakeAVCeleb with an unpublished item list, so the contamination guard refuses it on FakeAVCeleb. The only open audio-visual detector here; it needs at least 3.2 s of video with a face in all 16 sampled frames (too long for HiDF), and parity is not checked yet.
models.input: native-size face-box crops at 5 frames per second (up to 50), with the audio under them

paper.title: Leave No Stone Unturned: Uncovering Holistic Audio-Visual Intrinsic Coherence for Deepfake Detection

models.why: The only open audio-visual detector. v1 focuses on lip-sync with cloned voices, which only a model that checks whether voice and mouth agree can catch; MAVOS-DD Hindi is its South Asian test, and it is refused on FakeAVCeleb, which it was fine-tuned on.

models.name: LipForensics
models.summary: Lipreading-pretrained ResNet-18 and multi-scale temporal CNN on grayscale mouth crops, flagging unnatural mouth motion; LRW, then FF++ c23.
models.architecture: 25-frame clips of 96 px grayscale mouth crops (88 px centre crop), ResNet-18 with 3D stem, multi-scale temporal convolutional network, one logit per clip
models.description: LipForensics (Haliassos et al., CVPR 2021) is pretrained for lipreading on LRW, then its temporal network is fine-tuned on FaceForensics++ (c23, all four manipulations) to separate real from forged mouth motion, a high-level cue the authors argue survives unseen manipulations and compression. Central here because lip-sync fakes are a focus. Caveats: users report its FF++ numbers do not reproduce, it needs 25 consecutive frames with a detectable face, and parity is not checked yet.
models.input: mouth crops from 25 consecutive frames at a time (up to 100 frames per video)

paper.title: Lips Don't Lie: A Generalisable and Robust Approach to Face Forgery Detection

models.why: Looks only at the mouth, where lip-sync fakes, v1's focus, are edited. Tests whether FF++ face-swap detectors miss mouth-only edits on South Asian talking heads.

models.name: RECCE
models.summary: Xception encoder-decoder that reconstructs real faces only; reconstruction differences guide the classifier. DeepfakeBench weights, FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, Xception encoder with a decoder that reconstructs the face and guides attention from the reconstruction, two-way classifier
models.description: RECCE (Cao et al., CVPR 2022) trains a decoder to reconstruct real faces, so fakes reconstruct poorly, and uses the reconstruction differences to guide attention; the cue is not tied to one manipulation method. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23 per the DeepfakeBench README) after ImageNet pretraining. Passes parity against the original code.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: End-to-End Reconstruction-Classification Learning for Face Forgery Detection

models.why: Learns to reconstruct real faces only, so it tests whether its idea of a real face, learned from FF++, holds for South Asian faces. Like every DeepfakeBench detector here it trained on FF++, so each reads a different cue on the same faces; second tier, worth running once South Asian video arrives.

models.name: SBI
models.licence: research use only (commercial use needs a licence from the authors)
models.summary: EfficientNet-B4 trained on self-blended images (a real face blended with an altered copy of itself); real FF++ videos only, c23 checkpoint.
models.architecture: Face box widened by one eighth on each side and resized to 380 px, EfficientNet-B4 CNN, two-way classifier
models.description: SBI (Shiohara and Yamasaki, CVPR 2022) synthesises its training fakes by blending each real face with a slightly transformed copy of itself, producing the blending boundaries and statistical mismatches of face swaps without any real generator. Only FaceForensics++ real videos were used, after ImageNet pretraining; the c23 checkpoint is used here. Research-only licence, so its code is never copied into this repository.
models.input: 380 px face-box crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Detecting Deepfakes with Self-Blended Images

models.why: Trained on real faces blended into themselves, never on real deepfakes, so it depends least on its training set's faces and generators. The probe's test of whether that generalises better to South Asian faces and unseen generators.

models.name: SPSL
models.summary: Xception with the grey image's phase spectrum as a fourth input channel, where upsampling leaves traces; DeepfakeBench weights, FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, RGB plus phase spectrum of the grey image as a fourth channel, Xception CNN, two-way classifier
models.description: SPSL (Liu et al., CVPR 2021) adds the phase spectrum as an input channel beside RGB, since the upsampling in most face-forgery pipelines perturbs it. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23) after ImageNet pretraining and use the full Xception, not the paper's shallower network. The detector's yaml lists only FaceSwap, which may not describe the checkpoint; the benchmark treats it as trained on all of FF++.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Spatial-Phase Shallow Learning: Rethinking Face Forgery Detection in Frequency Domain

models.why: Reads the phase spectrum, where upsampling leaves traces whatever the face, so it tests a cue that shouldn't depend on skin tone. Like every DeepfakeBench detector here it trained on FF++, so each reads a different cue on the same faces; second tier, worth running once South Asian video arrives.

models.name: SRM
models.summary: Two-stream Xception: RGB plus SRM high-frequency noise residuals, coupled by cross-stream attention; DeepfakeBench weights, FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, RGB stream plus a stream of high-frequency noise residuals from SRM filters, Xception CNN with attention linking the two streams, two-way classifier
models.description: SRM (Luo et al., CVPR 2021) adds a stream of SRM-filtered high-frequency noise, where tampered and genuine regions differ, to avoid overfitting to method-specific colour textures, and lets the two streams guide each other with attention. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23 per the DeepfakeBench README) after ImageNet pretraining. Passes parity against the original code.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: Generalizing Face Forgery Detection with High-frequency Features

models.why: Reads high-frequency noise residuals, a cue sensitive to the phone cameras and compression typical of South Asian social media. Like every DeepfakeBench detector here it trained on FF++, so each reads a different cue on the same faces; second tier, worth running once South Asian video arrives.

models.name: UCF
models.summary: Xception encoders disentangle content, method-specific and common forgery features; only the common-forgery head scores. DeepfakeBench weights, FF++ c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, Xception encoders separating content, method-specific forgery and common forgery features, scored with the common-forgery head only
models.description: UCF (Yan et al., ICCV 2023) splits face features into forgery-irrelevant content, method-specific forgery and common forgery parts, and decides on the common part only, aiming at unseen manipulation methods. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on all four FaceForensics++ methods (c23) after ImageNet pretraining. Passes parity against the original code.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: UCF: Uncovering Common Features for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

models.why: Built to find forgery traces common to every generator, so it tests generalisation to the generators actually used in South Asia. Like every DeepfakeBench detector here it trained on FF++, so each reads a different cue on the same faces; second tier, worth running once South Asian video arrives.

models.name: Xception
models.summary: Xception (depthwise separable CNN) frame classifier on aligned face crops; the FF++ baseline, DeepfakeBench weights trained on c23.
models.architecture: Aligned 256 px face crop, Xception CNN with depthwise separable convolutions, two-way classifier
models.description: The face-forgery detector from the FaceForensics++ paper (Rossler et al., ICCV 2019), and the backbone the other DeepfakeBench detectors build on. DeepfakeBench's weights were trained on FaceForensics++ (c23 per the README; upstream issue 151, asking whether every checkpoint is c23, is unanswered) after ImageNet pretraining. Some users report the released weights do not reproduce DeepfakeBench's README table.
models.input: 256 px aligned face crops, 32 frames per video

paper.title: FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images

models.why: The most-cited video detector and the classic half of the video pair. Its training set, FF++, is dominated by lighter-skinned faces, so it measures what a standard detector does on South Asian skin tones.

models.name: XLS-R 300M + AASIST
models.summary: Fine-tuned XLS-R 300M front end with an AASIST graph-attention back end on its last layer; trained on ASVspoof 2019 LA only.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows, fine-tuned XLS-R 300M front end, AASIST graph attention back end on the last layer, two-way classifier
models.description: XLS-R + AASIST (Tak et al., Odyssey 2022) fine-tunes the SSL front end jointly with an AASIST back end. The front end was pretrained on real speech only (Common Voice, BABEL, MLS, VoxPopuli, VoxLingua107) and the detector trained on the ASVspoof 2019 LA training split alone, so with no MLAAD or FLEURS in training it is a clean zero-shot probe on South Asian sets. The adapter replaces fairseq and passes parity against upstream's own stack (2026-10-12).
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: Automatic speaker verification spoofing and deepfake detection using wav2vec 2.0 and data augmentation

published.cite: Table 3, best run with DF-tuned augmentation

models.why: The same training data as AASIST on a backbone pretrained on 128 languages: whether multilingual pretraining alone, with English-only fakes, carries over to South Asian speech. The foundation-model half of the probe's audio pair.

models.name: XLSR-Mamba
models.summary: Fine-tuned XLS-R 300M features read by a dual-column bidirectional Mamba back end instead of attention; trained on ASVspoof 2019 LA only.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows, fine-tuned XLS-R 300M front end, dual-column bidirectional Mamba back end (six blocks per direction), two-way classifier
models.description: XLSR-Mamba (Xiao and Das, IEEE SPL 2024) replaces the attention back end with forward and backward Mamba state space blocks over XLS-R features. The front end was pretrained on real speech (Common Voice, BABEL, MLS, VoxPopuli, VoxLingua107) and the released network trained on the ASVspoof 2019 LA training split alone. Here mamba-ssm's CUDA kernels are replaced by slower pure-PyTorch stand-ins, and parity against the kernels is not checked yet.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: XLSR-Mamba: A Dual-Column Bidirectional State Space Model for Spoofing Attack Detection

models.why: The same backbone and training as XLS-R + AASIST with a Mamba back end, so a failure the two share on South Asian speech points at the training data, not the head. Second tier.

models.name: XLS-R 300M + SLS
models.licence: none declared (code and weights); a Hugging Face mirror re-hosts the weights as MIT
models.summary: Fine-tuned XLS-R 300M with learned attention pooling over all 24 layers (Sensitive Layer Selection) and a small MLP; ASVspoof 2019 LA only.
models.architecture: Raw 16 kHz waveform in 64,600-sample windows, fine-tuned XLS-R 300M front end, learned attention over all 24 layers (SLS), two linear layers, two-way classifier
models.description: XLS-R + SLS (Zhang et al., ACM Multimedia 2024) weights every XLS-R layer with learned attention, since different layers carry different spoofing cues, before two linear layers. The front end was pretrained on real speech (Common Voice, BABEL, MLS, VoxPopuli, VoxLingua107) and the network trained on the ASVspoof 2019 LA training split alone, making it a clean zero-shot probe on every South Asian set. The repository declares no licence, so its code is imported, never copied; parity is not checked yet.
models.input: 4.04 s windows of raw 16 kHz audio

paper.title: Audio Deepfake Detection with Self-Supervised XLS-R and SLS Classifier

models.why: The same backbone and training as XLS-R + AASIST with a back end that pools every layer, so a failure the two share on South Asian speech points at the training data, not the head. Second tier.

datasets.name: ASVspoof 2019 Logical Access
datasets.licence: see LICENSE_text.txt on the DataShare page
datasets.summary: English VCTK speech, bona fide plus 19 TTS and voice-conversion attacks; the standard logical-access anti-spoofing benchmark.
datasets.scale: 7.6 GB; train, dev and eval with disjoint speakers
generators: 19 attack systems A01 to A19: text-to-speech, voice conversion, and TTS output passed through voice conversion (A13 to A15)
annotations: attack id: A01 to A19 (TTS, VC or TTS+VC)
official split: train, dev, eval (disjoint speakers)
datasets.format: FLAC, 16 kHz, 16-bit (VCTK downsampled)
datasets.notes: Train and dev share attacks A01 to A06; most eval attacks are unseen in training.

paper.title: ASVspoof 2019: A large-scale public database of synthesized, converted and replayed speech

datasets.why: Not South Asian. The reproduction set for the detectors trained on it: an adapter must match its published numbers here, and settle its score direction, before its South Asian numbers count, so a low South Asian AUC reads as a real failure rather than a flipped sign.

datasets.name: Bangla Audio Dataset, original and deepfake voices (Mendeley)
datasets.summary: Bangla read speech from 75 Bangladeshi speakers, each of 30 sentences read once and faked once, so every fake has a real twin.
annotations: gender: male, female (from the speaker folder)
real/fake twin: every fake has a real clip by the same speaker and sentence
datasets.format: WAV, 2 to 5 s clips
datasets.notes: The record never names the tool that made the fakes.
datasets.why: Bangladeshi Bengali with every fake paired to the same speaker's real clip and a gender label, so it separates the fake from speaker and recording differences and gives the gender comparison.

datasets.name: BanglaFake
datasets.summary: Bengali real speech and VITS text-to-speech fakes in three sub-corpora (sust, mozilla, news).
annotations: speaker id (mozilla sub-corpus only, five Common Voice speakers)
datasets.format: WAV, 22.05 kHz, 6 to 7 s clips
datasets.notes: The news sub-corpus is real only, and the archive's counts differ from the README's.

paper.title: BanglaFake: Constructing and Evaluating a Specialized Bengali Deepfake Audio Dataset

datasets.why: The largest open Bengali set, with sub-corpora recorded in different ways, so results can be split by recording condition.

datasets.name: BD-GRF6 (Bangladeshi real and fake speech, three genders)
datasets.summary: Bangla real and fake speech by Bangladeshi speakers, grouped male, female and third gender; the only set with a third-gender group.
datasets.format: WAV and MP3 (format differs by class)
datasets.notes: Third-gender real clips are MP3 while female fakes are WAV, so file format can leak the label.
datasets.why: Bangladeshi speech with a third-gender group, which Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan recognise in law: the only set that tests gender beyond male and female. Cross-corpus until its file formats are checked, since they may give the label away.

datasets.name: Casual Conversations v2
datasets.summary: Real video only: consenting participants in seven countries (India the largest), with self-reported and annotated demographics; for false positives on real faces.
annotations: skin tone: Fitzpatrick and Monk scales (annotated)
datasets.format: video, 26,467 recordings, about 674 h in all
datasets.notes: Real videos only; some labels are licensed for evaluation use only.

paper.title: The Casual Conversations v2 Dataset : A diverse, large benchmark for measuring fairness and robustness in audio/vision/speech models

datasets.why: Real video only, with India its largest country and self-reported demographics: how often detectors flag real South Asian faces as fake, the harm that falls on real people.

datasets.name: Celeb-DF (v2)
datasets.summary: Celebrity face-swap videos from YouTube made with an improved DeepFake synthesis process; a standard cross-dataset video test.
generators: DeepFake face swap with the authors' improved synthesis process
datasets.format: MP4
datasets.notes: About 88% of subjects are Caucasian, so it carries no South Asian signal.

paper.title: Celeb-DF: A Large-Scale Challenging Dataset for DeepFake Forensics

datasets.why: Not South Asian (mostly Caucasian subjects). A video reproduction set: it or FF++ settles every video model's score direction, without which no video number counts.

datasets.name: Deepfake-Eval-2024
datasets.summary: In-the-wild real and fake video, audio and images collected from social media in 2024, in 52 languages.
generators: in the wild, unknown tools; manipulation types include lip-sync, face swap and diffusion (per the paper)
datasets.format: video about 30 fps, average 576 x 720 px, about 80 s average; audio about 44.7 kHz, about 115 s average; images mostly 1024 x 1024
datasets.notes: Evaluation only, no training on it; its metadata columns are unverified until access is granted.

paper.title: Deepfake-Eval-2024: A Multi-Modal In-the-Wild Benchmark of Deepfakes Circulated in 2024

datasets.why: Picked as the only set of deepfakes that actually circulated online. It has no country field, so South Asian items can't be picked out, and access requests are often rejected.

datasets.name: DeePhy
datasets.summary: Face-swap videos with one to three successive swaps (FaceShifter, FaceSwap, FSGAN), for attributing the sequence of generators.
annotations: swap succession: one, two or three successive swaps
facial hair, spectacles, shades, mic and head or hair occlusion attributes
datasets.format: MP4, 720p, 25 fps, about 20 s
datasets.notes: Only 100 real videos against 5,040 fakes.

paper.title: DeePhy: On Deepfake Phylogeny

datasets.why: Indian face swaps with up to three successive generators, so South Asian faces under several generators. With few real videos it measures misses more than false alarms.

datasets.name: DF-Platter
datasets.summary: Indian face-swap videos (FSGAN, FaceShifter, FaceSwap), single- and multi-subject, labelled by gender, age, skin tone and occlusion.
annotations: set: A (single subject), B and C (multiple subjects)
datasets.format: videos at low and high resolution, c0, c23 and c40 compression
datasets.notes: Its licence limits use to research colleagues at the signing institution.

paper.title: DF-Platter: Multi-Face Heterogeneous Deepfake Dataset

datasets.why: The largest Indian video set, labelled by skin tone, gender, age and occlusion: where skin- tone effects on South Asian faces can be measured directly.

datasets.name: FakeAVCeleb
datasets.licence: non-commercial research and education (site says CC BY 4.0; the GitHub README defers to the request form)
datasets.summary: VoxCeleb2 celebrity videos with fake video, fake audio or both, across five ethnic groups including 100 South Asian real videos.
annotations: category: RealVideo-RealAudio, RealVideo-FakeAudio, FakeVideo-RealAudio, FakeVideo-FakeAudio (which track is fake)
ethnicity: African, Asian (East), Asian (South), Caucasian (American), Caucasian (European)
datasets.format: MP4 from VoxCeleb2, about 7.8 s on average
datasets.notes: Ethnicity and gender come from the folder layout, which is unverified until a copy arrives.

paper.title: FakeAVCeleb: A Novel Audio-Video Multimodal Deepfake Dataset

datasets.why: The only set with a South Asian group beside four other ethnic groups under one recording setup, so it gives the probe's South Asian against others comparison. Its speech is English.

datasets.name: FaceForensics++
datasets.summary: 1,000 real YouTube videos and their fakes from face-swap and face-reenactment methods; the standard video training set and in-domain test.
datasets.scale: 1,000 real videos plus fakes, about 40 GB
annotations: target id and source id of each fake
official split: train, val, test (JSON pair lists)
datasets.format: MP4, c23 compression used here (raw and c40 also exist)
datasets.notes: Real videos come from 977 YouTube videos, mostly frontal faces.

paper.title: FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images

datasets.why: Not South Asian. Every video detector here trained on it, so its test split is where video adapters reproduce published numbers and settle score direction.

datasets.name: HiDF (human-indistinguishable deepfakes), videos
datasets.summary: Commercial-tool face swaps selected because people cannot tell them from real, with race labels including an Indian group.
generators: commercial face-swap tools (which tool made which video is not stated)
annotations: race: White, Asian, Latino, Black, Indian
datasets.format: MP4 with audio, 512 px face crops, about 3 s
datasets.notes: Clips are too short for HAVIC's 3.2 s windows, and the 62k images are not fetched.

paper.title: HiDF: A Human-Indistinguishable Deepfake Dataset

datasets.why: Not South Asian, but race-labelled with an Indian group: a stopgap check of false alarms on real faces by race until South Asian video arrives. Its Indian group is small, so it should step back once FakeAVCeleb or DF-Platter is in.

datasets.name: IAV-DF
datasets.summary: Indian audio-video deepfakes: motion-model reenactment, face swaps and Wav2Lip lip-sync with cloned voices.
datasets.notes: Only a sample was ever released and its link is dead, so nothing can be downloaded.
datasets.why: Picked because it is Indian lip-sync with cloned voices, exactly v1's type. Dropped: its only sample link is dead.

datasets.name: In-the-Wild (Müller et al. 2022)
datasets.summary: Real and fake English speech of public figures collected from the internet; the standard out-of-domain audio test.
datasets.format: WAV, 37.9 h in all (20.7 h real, 17.2 h fake)
datasets.notes: meta.csv lists 54 speakers while the card says 58 celebrities and politicians.

paper.title: Does Audio Deepfake Detection Generalize?

datasets.why: Not South Asian. Real-world English deepfakes of public figures: the reproduction set where the guard refuses ASVspoof (DF Arena, AntiDeepfake), and the out-of-domain reference South Asian scores are compared with.

datasets.name: InDeepFake
datasets.summary: Indian YouTube videos in seven languages with face swaps and text-to-speech plus Wav2Lip lip-sync fakes.
annotations: language: English, Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Tamil, Punjabi, Rajasthani
datasets.format: video excerpts of about 10 to 12 s from YouTube
datasets.notes: Access is restricted to academic institutions on request.

paper.title: InDeepFake: A novel multimodal multilingual indian deepfake video dataset

datasets.why: Indian YouTube video in seven languages with face swaps and TTS plus Wav2Lip lip-sync: South Asian talking heads with cloned voices, close to v1's type.

datasets.name: Indic-CodecFake
datasets.summary: Fakes made by re-encoding IndicSUPERB speech in 12 Indian languages with neural audio codecs (DAC, Encodec).
generators: DAC neural audio codec (16, 24 and 44 kHz)
Encodec neural audio codec (24 and 48 kHz)
datasets.notes: No download exists yet; its real side is IndicSUPERB.

paper.title: Indic-CodecFake meets SATYAM: Towards Detecting Neural Audio Codec Synthesized Speech Deepfakes in Indic Languages

datasets.why: Picked as Indian-language fakes from neural audio codecs, a kind of fake no other set covers. Dropped: no download exists.

datasets.name: IndicSUPERB (Kathbath)
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 (the Hugging Face card of ai4bharat/Kathbath; the IndicSUPERB code repo is Apache-2.0)
datasets.summary: Real read speech in 12 Indian languages (Kathbath); the real counterpart for IndicSynth, sharing its speaker ids.
datasets.format: m4a
datasets.notes: Only the clean test splits are fetched; the 85 GB train split is left out.

paper.title: IndicSUPERB: A Speech Processing Universal Performance Benchmark for Indian languages

datasets.why: Real read speech in 12 Indian languages from the speakers IndicSynth clones, so IndicSynth's evalsets pair each fake with real speech from the same speakers and corpus.

datasets.name: IndicSynth
datasets.summary: Fake-only speech in 12 Indian languages from XTTS-v2, VITS and FreeVC24, cloning IndicSUPERB speakers.
datasets.format: WAV embedded in parquet rows
datasets.notes: Fake only; real speech comes from IndicSUPERB. Shards are sorted by generator, so small samples may miss some.

paper.title: IndicSynth: A Large-Scale Multilingual Synthetic Speech Dataset for Low-Resource Indian Languages

datasets.why: The largest open South Asian fake speech, with voice conversion (FreeVC24) beside TTS: the cloned-voice half of v1, with generator and gender labels.

datasets.name: IndicTTS Deepfake Challenge data
datasets.summary: Real and text-to-speech clips in 16 Indian languages, including Nepali, from a Hugging Face community challenge.
annotations: speaker code and gender (from the id)
official split: train, test (test labels hidden)
datasets.format: 16 kHz audio embedded in parquet rows
datasets.notes: The card names neither the TTS system nor where the real speech comes from.
datasets.why: Sixteen Indian languages and the only labelled Nepali fakes in one set, so it is where language becomes a per-group attribute.

datasets.name: IndieFake
datasets.summary: Indian-accented English from 50 speakers: real recordings and voice-cloned fakes of hypothetical, same-speaker and cross-speaker transcripts.
generators: voice cloning with tools such as Amazon Polly, Play.ht or ElevenLabs
annotations: background: celebrity, politician, academic, businessman, member of the public
datasets.format: WAV, 16 kHz, about 5 s on average
datasets.notes: Indian-accented English only, no South Asian languages.

paper.title: IndieFake Dataset: A Benchmark Dataset for Audio Deepfake Detection

datasets.why: Indian-accented English with voices cloned across speakers: voice-cloning scams in the English South Asian public figures often speak.

datasets.name: LRLspoof (low-resource language spoofs)
datasets.summary: Fake-only speech in 66 low-resource languages, including Nepali and Assamese, from 24 open-source TTS systems; deferred.
datasets.format: WAV, shipped as one gzipped tarball in 47 parts
datasets.notes: Spoof only, and no language can be fetched without the whole 462 GB archive.

paper.title: When Spoof Detectors Travel: Evaluation Across 66 Languages in the Low-Resource Language Spoofing Corpus

datasets.why: More Nepali and Assamese fakes from 24 TTS systems, where Nepali data is thinnest. Deferred: no language can be fetched without the whole 462 GB archive.

datasets.name: MAVOS-DD, Hindi subset
datasets.summary: Hindi YouTube videos and fakes from eight face-swap, talking-head, reenactment and voice-conversion generators; our one downloadable South Asian audio-video set.
annotations: which track was manipulated: video, audio
datasets.format: MP4, 256 x 256 to 1920 x 1080, 23 to 60 fps, audio 16 to 44.1 kHz
datasets.notes: The paper says face swaps keep their source audio, but the repo leaves the audio label of non-knnvc fakes null until the metadata confirms it.

paper.title: MAVOS-DD: Multilingual Audio-Video Open-Set Deepfake Detection Benchmark

datasets.why: The only South Asian video anyone can download: Hindi talking heads, face swaps and voice conversion, so it is the first test of v1's lip-sync with cloned voices, and HAVIC's only South Asian set.

datasets.name: Comprehensive Deepfake Detection Dataset: Real and Synthetic Frames from Roop and Akool (Mendeley v3)
datasets.summary: Face-crop frames of Bangladeshi and Indian people, real and faked with Roop and Akool.
annotations: technique: Tech-1, Tech-2 (which is Roop and which Akool is not stated)
name of the person swapped in (file name)
datasets.format: JPEG face crops, 500 x 500, frames taken at 5 fps
datasets.notes: Pipeline test only, never reported; frames of one video are near-duplicates, so never split them across train and test.
datasets.why: Bangladeshi and Indian face crops faked with consumer tools: a pipeline test, used for video parity checks, never for results.

datasets.name: MLAAD
datasets.summary: Fake-only text-to-speech in many languages (Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Urdu, Sinhala and more), synthesised from M-AILABS source text.
datasets.scale: 1,000 clips per language and generator, 9.5 GB
generators: text-to-speech systems, one folder each (Hindi 9, Bengali 4, Kannada 2, one each for Tamil, Marathi, Urdu, Sinhala, Malayalam)
datasets.format: WAV
datasets.notes: Fake only; real speech must come from another corpus, so every evalset on it is cross-corpus.

paper.title: MLAAD: The Multi-Language Audio Anti-Spoofing Dataset

datasets.why: The only Sinhala deepfake speech anywhere, plus Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and Urdu. Fake only, so its evalsets are cross-corpus and diagnostic until the shortcut probe clears them.

datasets.name: Large Sinhala ASR training data (OpenSLR SLR52)
datasets.summary: Google's crowd-sourced Sinhala read speech, real only; the real half for MLAAD's Sinhala fakes.
datasets.format: FLAC
datasets.notes: No gender labels, and only the first of 16 zips is fetched.

paper.title: Crowd-Sourced Speech Corpora for Javanese, Sundanese, Sinhala, Nepali, and Bangladeshi Bengali

datasets.why: Real Sinhala read speech, the real half for MLAAD's Sinhala fakes: the only way to test Sri Lanka's main language today.

datasets.name: SEA-Spoof (Hindi and Tamil parts)
datasets.licence: other (non-commercial academic research only; the paper says CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
datasets.summary: Real and fake speech in seven languages (Hindi and Tamil used here) from six open TTS systems and four commercial voice tools.
datasets.format: FLAC, 16 kHz, in parquet shards
datasets.notes: The schema comes from the card and paper; nobody on the team has seen the files yet.

paper.title: SEA-Spoof: Bridging The Gap in Multilingual Audio Deepfake Detection for South-East Asian

datasets.why: Hindi and Tamil fakes from named commercial voice tools as well as open TTS, the kind of tools behind real scams.

datasets.name: SpeechFake (South Asian languages)
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 (README; ModelScope metadata says Apache-2.0)
datasets.summary: Multilingual real and fake speech; we use Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Marathi and Malayalam, faked mostly with Edge-TTS, plus SeedVC for Hindi.
datasets.scale: 143 GB for the South Asian parts
datasets.format: WAV, 16 kHz mono, mostly 2 to 20 s
datasets.notes: The paper promises transcripts and voice ids, but the metadata CSVs we read carry only label, generator kind, model and language.

paper.title: SpeechFake: A Large-Scale Multilingual Speech Deepfake Dataset Incorporating Cutting-Edge Generation Methods

datasets.why: More Indic fakes (Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Marathi, Malayalam) from a free, widely used TTS and from voice conversion. Cross-corpus, so diagnostic until the shortcut probe.

datasets.name: Svarah (Indian-accented English)
datasets.licence: none declared on the Hugging Face card (AI4Bharat)
datasets.summary: Real Indian-accented English from 117 speakers across India, labelled by gender, age, state and first language; for false positives.
datasets.format: audio embedded in parquet, test split only
datasets.notes: No licence is declared, so nothing derived from it is published yet.

paper.title: Svarah: Evaluating English ASR Systems on Indian Accents

datasets.why: Real Indian-accented English from across India with gender, age, state and first language: false alarms on real South Asian voices, split by region.

datasets.name: UniDataPro deepfake videos (free Hugging Face preview)
datasets.summary: Free preview: five real phone videos and five face-swap fakes made from them.
generators: magichour.ai (which service made which fake is not stated)
annotations: pairing of real video, fake and source face image (CSV)
datasets.format: MP4 and MOV phone videos with audio, 480p to 1080p
datasets.notes: Pipeline test only, never reported; whether the fakes keep the original audio is unknown.
datasets.why: A tiny free preview of phone videos and their face swaps: a pipeline test, never reported.

datasets.name: Urdu Deepfake Audio (CSALT-LUMS)
datasets.summary: Urdu speech from 17 speakers: real clips and matched fakes from two TTS systems (VITS and Tacotron).
datasets.format: WAV
datasets.notes: This release has 6,794 clips, far fewer than the paper's 20,451 real and 16,830 fake utterances.

paper.title: Deepfake Defense: Constructing and Evaluating a Specialized Urdu Deepfake Audio Dataset

datasets.why: Pakistan's Urdu with generator labels (VITS, Tacotron), the first South Asian set scored. It behaves unlike the others, which makes it the test case for recording artefacts.
